label: First sleepover

what_happens.title: What happens at a sleepover
goals: The steps: pack the bag, arrive and say hello, play, dinner, pyjamas, bedtime, breakfast, pick-up
A sleepover means sleeping one night at a friend's or family member's home
Pick-up time is set, and the grown-up comes back
what_happens.parentSkill: Tell your child the exact pick-up time and who comes, and say it the same way each night.

who_is_there.title: Who is at the sleepover
goals: The host grown-ups are in charge and know what to do
The friend or cousin and maybe a pet
The child can always ask the host grown-up for help or a call home
who_is_there.parentSkill: Introduce the host grown-up by name, and agree with them how a call home works.

what_i_do.title: What I do at the sleepover
goals: Play, eat, brush teeth and put on pyjamas
Say what I need: a night light, the toilet, a drink of water
Use my own bedtime steps with my toy
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise asking: 'Where is the toilet?' and 'Can I have the light on?'

if_scared.title: If I miss home at night
goals: A different bed, dark room and new night sounds
Missing home is normal, and it often passes
Calm tools: the toy from home, a note in the bag, slow breaths, asking for a call
if_scared.parentSkill: Agree an honest plan for missing home, including whether you can come early, and keep it.

rehearsal.title: Let's practise the sleepover
goals: Have a pretend sleepover in the living room
Say the steps once more, ending with breakfast and pick-up
rehearsal.parentSkill: Do a practice sleepover at home: different room, own bag, own bedtime steps.

steps: Pack my bag: pyjamas, toothbrush, my toy
Arrive and say hello to the host grown-ups
Brush teeth, put on pyjamas and get ready for bed
Sleep in a different bed with my toy
[[GROWNUP]] picks me up at the time we agreed
sensory: a different bed and a different pillow
a dark room with new shadows
new night sounds, like a fridge humming or a pet moving
my own blanket or toy that smells like home
honestyNotes: A first sleepover can end early, and that is fine. Do not promise the child will not miss home. Agree honestly with your child and the host about calls and early pick-up, and keep the promise you make.

fallbackAnswer: Missing home is normal, and lots of kids feel it at night.
You can hug your toy, read the note in your bag, or ask the grown-up there for help.
[[GROWNUP]] comes after breakfast, at the time we agreed.
We can say the time together so you remember it.
We will agree a plan for calling home before you go.
The grown-ups there know the plan too.
You can ask for a night light or for the door open a little.
Your toy from home will be right there.
The grown-ups at your friend's home look after you all night.
You can ask them for anything you need.

questionButtons.text: What if I need the toilet at night?
fallbackAnswer: Before bed, ask where the toilet is so you know the way.
You can wake a grown-up if you need help.

questionButtons.text: What if I don't like the food?
fallbackAnswer: You can say, no thank you, politely.
There will be other things to eat, and breakfast is coming too.
You might play games, watch a film, or build a blanket fort.

techniques.label: Bringing a comfort toy
techniques.how: Pack the toy or blanket your child sleeps with; it carries the smell of home.

techniques.label: A note in the bag
techniques.how: Hide a short note or drawing in the bag for bedtime, with a heart and the pick-up time.

techniques.label: An agreed call plan
techniques.how: Agree with your child and the host when a call home happens and what happens if your child wants to come home.

techniques.label: My own bedtime steps
techniques.how: Tell the host your child's bedtime steps and let your child do them the same way.

techniques.label: A practice sleepover at home
techniques.how: Sleep in a different room at home, or at a grandparent's, before the real night.

techniques.label: Practising asking for help
techniques.how: Practise 'Can I have a drink of water?', 'Where is the toilet?' and 'Can the light stay on?'

techniques.label: A night light
techniques.how: Pack a small night light or ask the host to leave one on.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

ritual: Pack my bag and my toy
Play, pyjamas and my bedtime steps

pain: If your tummy feels funny, tell the grown-up there.
Missing home can feel like a sore heart. A hug from your toy helps.
separation: I come after breakfast, at the time we said.
Your toy from home stays with you all night.
unknown: First play, then dinner, then pyjamas, then bed, then breakfast, then me.
strangers: The grown-ups there look after you all night. You can ask them anything.
sensory: A night light or an open door can help with the dark.
New houses have new night sounds, like humming fridges.
safety: We have a plan for calling home, and the grown-ups know it.
You can always ask for help, even at night.
social: You and your friend can build a blanket fort.
Lots of kids feel shy at first. It gets easier.
body: Ask where the toilet is before bed.
You can ask for a drink of water.
love: I love you, even when we are in different houses.
I am proud of you for trying.
